links.targetTitle: The derecognition record shows operational security breaches
No adjudication process exists for misalignment by Ecosystem
The Atlas admits it lacks fact-finding and evidence protocol

title: The Atlas concedes its adjudicator may lack the expertise to judge operational security breaches
content:
NR-4 opens with an admission that sits awkwardly against A.1.5.7's severity: "The Core Facilitator may not have the needed experience and skills to adjudicate matters involving operational security best practices."

The proposal it carries — quoted from a Facilitator team forum post on an actual AD derecognition for an opsec breach — is to retain a security firm as a Scope Advisor to "thoroughly analyze the security needs and risks of the Alignment Conservers and develop ever-evolving Operational Security 'Best Practices'." Two distinct benefits are claimed, and they matter to different parties:

1. **For the governed**: "With an explicit framework of agreed-upon Best Practices, all anon Alignment Conservers have a known target to meet." Under A.1.5.7 an opsec failure ends a career permanently, so the absence of a published standard means an unbounded obligation with an irreversible penalty.
2. **For the adjudicator**: "The explicit framework removes the risk of the Facilitator inappropriately inserting subjective bias into the decision-making process." An objective benchmark protects the judge from the suspicion that the standard was set after the fact.

The advisor is also floated as an evidence evaluator — assessing an informant's evidence for "validity/quality" and whether "the methods used by the informant to secure the evidence were ethical," under confidentiality.

The generalizable point is that this is the second place in the Governance Scope where a severe, mandatory sanction is already in force while the standard it enforces is acknowledged as undeveloped (compare NR-1 and NR-8 on fact-finding and evidence). The pattern is consistent: the Atlas installs the consequence first, because the risk is live, and files the missing rigor as research.
description: NR-4 proposes hiring a Security Scope Advisor to author objective opsec best practices, both to give ACs a knowable target and to keep facilitator subjectivity out of breach determinations.
